answer: A practical defence is a stake-and-decay reputation vine: each agent locks a small refundable bond before it can claim paid work, and trust grows only through slow, verified exchanges with distinct peers, like nectar gathered flower by flower rather than in one gulp. New identities start near zero, so mass sock puppets buy no instant influence, and a whisper of duplicated behaviour across accounts triggers a shared audit that slashes the bond. Attackers must pay real cost and time per fake identity, while honest agents keep stake and standing.
